#4848. The 7 Best Garmin Watches, Tested by Our Fitness and Tech Experts

Garmin has a watch for every type of athlete and budget.

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

Brands like Whoop, OURA, and Apple offer some of the best fitness trackers available, but Garmin watches remain the go-to for serious athletes and outdoor enthusiasts. Men’s Health editors have trusted these wearables to go the distance during ultramarathons, multi-day hikes, and backcountry ski trips thanks to their weeks-long battery life and pinpoint GPS accuracy. But they’re equally useful for everyday life and weekend warriors—we love wearing the Garmin Approach S70 for golf rounds because it comes preloaded with more than 43,000 courses from around the world.

The current Garmin lineup is more robust than ever, from entry-level running watches to premium expedition-ready models that cost upwards of $1,000. Several models come with full-color topographic maps, military-grade durability, and hardcore activity-specific metrics. For instance, runners get detailed stride analysis, cyclists receive power metrics, and swimmers enjoy stroke detection. They also offer specialized outdoor capabilities, including barometric altimeters for precise elevation tracking, compass sensors for navigation without GPS, and pulse oximeters that help monitor your acclimation at high altitudes.

The Garmin Vivoactive 6 offers health monitoring features like sleep coaching, recovery time recommendations, and training readiness scores. Meanwhile, adventure-focused models like the Garmin Instinct 3 and Garmin Fenix 8 Pro incorporate multi-band GPS for accuracy in dense forests, plus emergency features like fall detection and SOS alerts. Whether you’re tracking your first 5K or planning a summit attempt on a remote peak, there’s a Garmin designed specifically for your needs. We’ve logged thousands of miles testing these watches to help you find the perfect match.

Over the years, our editors have done it all: ultramarathons, multi-day backpacking trips, open water swims, and mountain expeditions. Through our adventures, Garmin watches have consistently proven their worth on our wrists. To find the best Garmin watches, we evaluated several models across multiple activities, testing their GPS accuracy, battery performance, and usability. We also considered factors like comfort during prolonged wear and durability when subjected to the elements. This testing allowed us to see how each watch performs out in the real world beyond the spec sheet.

The Fenix 8 stands as Garmin’s ultimate performance watch, offering detailed training insights and reliability for marathoners, ultra-runners, and multi-sport competitors. The watch doesn’t doesn’t track your runs—it analyzes every aspect of your performance with features like training readiness, recovery time, and PacePro technology, allowing you to plan your race-day strategy with GPS-based pace guidance. These features can help you optimize your performance.

Battery life remains exceptional even during GPS-intensive activities. While the standard 51mm AMOLED version delivers approximately 29 days, the solar-equipped model extends this to 48 days with adequate sun exposure. The watch offers multiple power management profiles that let you customize battery usage based on what you have planned that day. This ensures you have the data you need from start to finish without worrying about mid-race charging.

Beyond its training capabilities, the Fenix 8 serves as a reliable navigation tool during unfamiliar routes and trail races. The full-color topographic maps, turn-by-turn directions, and ClimbPro feature help you strategize your effort on challenging courses. You also get comprehensive recovery features, with detailed sleep tracking, HRV status, and body battery energy monitoring that help prevent overtraining.

While the Fenix 8’s price places it among the most expensive sport watches available (especially for the new Fenix 8 Pro), serious athletes who spend hundreds of hours training for major events will find the watch’s performance insights and bulletproof reliability well worth the investment. "This watch has everything that Garmin has to offer into a low-profile casing," says MH Fitness and Commerce Editor Charles Thorp, NASM. "Rugged enough to perform in tough terrain, but sleek enough to fit in everywhere else."

The Vivoactive 6 is one of Garmin’s more lifestyle-oriented models, offering a balance between everyday smartwatch functionality and robust fitness tracking. With its sleek design and comprehensive tracking features, it’s a solid alternative to the Apple Watch SE for those who want longer battery life (up to 11 days) and more comprehensive fitness metrics.

Through running and strength training sessions, the Vivoactive 6 offers detailed metrics about VO2 max, aerobic and anaerobic output, and exercise load. These insights provide a clearer picture of fitness progress than basic calorie and distance tracking. The responsiveness during workouts particularly stood out during our side-by-side comparison with the Apple Watch SE. When increasing running pace, the Vivoactive 6 updated immediately, while the Apple Watch lagged noticeably behind. During strength training, we appreciated the live heart rate zone updates, making it easier to gauge workout intensity in real time.

The most significant advantage over the Apple Watch is battery life. While our SE required daily charging, the Vivoactive 6 kept going for days between charges—a game-changer for active users. The comfortable fit works well even on smaller wrists, and at $299, it offers more fitness functionality than similarly priced competitors while maintaining everyday usability. It supports contactless payments and can even store music from your favorite Spotify playlists. If you want comprehensive fitness insights without the premium price, the Vivoactive 6 hits the sweet spot.

The Forerunner 970 is Garmin’s new flagship running watch, built for athletes who want every data point without sacrificing everyday usability. It pairs a brighter 1.4-inch AMOLED display with a built-in speaker and microphone, plus a tougher sapphire lens and lightweight titanium bezel, so it feels premium yet rugged enough for hard training.

During intervals and long runs, the interface is intuitive—pace, heart rate, and distance are all visible at a glance, and after each session the watch prompts you to rate how the run felt. The 970 also offers deeper performance tools, including running economy, running tolerance (when paired with Garmin’s HRM 600 chest strap), hill score, endurance score, and more detailed load analysis to show how hard you’re pushing week to week.

Battery life remains a major selling point. Garmin claims up to 15 days in smartwatch mode and 26 hours in GPS mode with multi-band SATIQ, so you can stack long runs, races, and daily training without worrying about charging. Built-in full-color maps, turn-by-turn directions, dynamic round-trip routing, ClimbPro, and Up Ahead make the watch just as useful on unfamiliar trails as it is for neighborhood miles.

Recovery and health tracking also see significant upgrades over older Forerunners. Training Readiness delivers a simple morning score based on recent sleep and workload, so you know whether to push or back off. Upgraded sleep tracking, nap detection, and newer tools like ECG readings also provide a clearer picture of how your body handles stress, illness, and heavy training weeks.

If you’re looking for something that’s durable, look no further than the Instinct 3. The watch offers military-grade construction that can withstand some real punishment, with a rugged design that proved its worth throughout testing. We accidentally banged it against doorways and scraped it against kettlebells during workouts, yet it emerged without a scratch. The distinctly masculine aesthetic features a substantial case housing an impressive array of sensors while maintaining water resistance to 100 meters.

Battery performance is one of the Instinct 3’s most impressive features. While Garmin claims 18 days between charges, our testing revealed closer to 21 days of regular use without heavy reliance on battery-intensive features. It makes it one of the longest-lasting watches in Garmin’s lineup, while providing a significant advantage over other mainstream smartwatches. When you do need a recharge, a quick 10-minute session can add several hours of use—perfect for those who forgot to charge before heading out the door.

For trail runs and hikers, the watch includes a digital compass that shows your precise directional heading, multi-band GPS with SatIQ technology, and a built-in flashlight with multiple intensity levels including a red light option. The Instinct 3 also features ABC sensors that provide real-time environmental data. Of course, the watch also offers powerful health and fitness features, including HRV status, stress tracking, and the ability to track your blood oxygen levels.

Read more: Our Garmin Instinct 3 AMOLED Review

Don’t let the lower price tag fool you: The Forerunner 165 packs serious running tech into a $249 package, making it the ideal option for runners who are just getting started on their journey or those looking to dip their toes into fitness trackers. This relative newcomer to Garmin’s lineup boasts an AMOLED display, a lightweight design, and advanced training metrics runners will appreciate.

Despite being positioned as an entry-level running watch, the Forerunner 165 outclasses similarly priced competitors with its premium build quality and thoughtful design. It’s incredibly comfortable, especially compared to Garmin’s bulkier models, while still maintaining the brand’s impressive durability. The AMOLED screen offers excellent readability even in bright sunlight, and text looks crisp. We particularly appreciated the intuitive physical button navigation combined with touchscreen functionality.

For runners who want their first serious training companion, the Forerunner 165 hits the sweet spot by delivering Garmin’s core running analytics without overwhelming users. While it lacks some of the advanced recovery tools found in the Forerunner 965 like Training Readiness, it covers all the essentials with accurate GPS tracking and guided workouts.

The Venu 4 is Garmin’s latest lifestyle smartwatch, and it feels like a smarter, more polished upgrade from the Venu 3. Available in 41mm and 45mm sizes, it pairs a bright AMOLED display with a metal case and a low-profile design for a clean, casual look that looks great both at the office and at the gym.

In testing, the Venu line has always stood out for being easy to live with, and the latest model doubles down on that. Battery life stretches up to roughly 12 days in smartwatch mode depending on how often you’re working out and using the always-on display, which means you don’t have to baby it with nightly charges—topping it up during a shower a few times a week is usually enough. The built-in LED flashlight is also a welcome addition for running at dusk or dawn, helping you stay visible to drivers. You also get a speaker and mic for taking calls and using your phone’s voice assistant from your wrist.

What makes the Venu 4 more than a standard smartwatch is that it treats your health as more than just steps and heart rate. Health status and lifestyle logging show how daily choices—like drinking caffeine later in the day—actually affect your sleep, stress, and heart rate variability, so the data feels more useful than just a bunch of charts. The Venu 4 also has the new Garmin Coach feature, with over 80 preloaded GPS and indoor sports apps that cover everything from walking and HIIT to yoga and strength training.

Its app and ecosystem integration still isn’t as far-reaching as an Apple Watch, especially on iPhone, but if you care more about deeper health tracking and better workouts, the Venu 4 is a great alternative that offers multi-day battery life and more recovery-focused insights.

The Approach S70 is the ultimate golf companion, delivering comprehensive course coverage—with over 43,000 preloaded courses worldwide—in a sleek, lightweight design. Available in two sizes (42mm and 47mm), this premium golf watch displays detailed course maps showing precise distance to greens, hazards, and doglegs, while the Virtual Caddie feature provides club recommendations based on your playing history and current conditions.

What truly sets the S70 apart is its attention to golf-specific details. The watch provides front, center, and back distance readings to every green, along with precise yardages to hazards. This is extremely helpful as sometimes you can’t even fully see a hole and have no idea that a water hazard is lying within distance of your next shot, so that overview of the hole is crucial info to have. The "plays like" feature accounts for elevation changes and wind when calculating distances, something that can be difficult to gauge on your own.

Beyond the thousands of preloaded courses, the S70 also displays green contour data to improve your putting strategy (Garmin Golf membership required). During our testing, the functions and how to navigate them took a little getting used to, but once we got that down, it was pretty easy after every shot just to twist our wrist to get our next distance. The AMOLED display has also been crisp and never difficult to see out in the sun.

At $699, the S70 is a significant investment, but for golfers who regularly play and want and easy way to gauge the shots to hit, the combination of golf-specific features and modern smartwatch functionality makes it a great companion on the course.

Read More: Our Review of the Garmin Approach S70

Depending on the Garmin you choose, you can expect battery life to last anywhere from a few days to a few weeks. The Fenix 8 AMOLED’s battery can stretch for up to 16 days, while the Fenix 8 with solar will go up to 21 days (28 days with solar). Of course, real-world battery performance can vary based on how you actually use your watch. Running a marathon with continuous GPS tracking? You’ll drain the battery much faster than if you’re just checking notifications and tracking daily steps.

Garmin has a reputation for offering several advanced training and recovery metrics, which can help you understand how ready your body is for exercise and optimize your training schedule. The Forerunner 970 offers Training Readiness, which synthesizes your sleep score, recovery time, acute training load, sleep history, and more to show "when you are most likely to benefit from a hard workout and when to consider dialing down to let your body catch up," Garmin says.Even if you don’t train every day, you can still benefit from Garmin’s more basic tracking features, like daily step count, calories, and sleep. Some models can even track your stress, monitoring your body’s physiological responses throughout the day. During a hectic workday or high-pressure meeting, knowing when you’re stressed can prompt you to take action—i.e., perform breathing exercises—which can make a difference in your overall well-being.Additionally, Garmin’s various models analyze detailed performance metrics to determine if your training is productive, offer built-in coaching features to prepare you for races, and suggest workouts tailored to your fitness level and goals. What makes Garmin’s approach so good is its flexibility—serious athletes can drive into the data, while casual users can stick with simpler metrics and guided programs.

GPS and Garmin go hand in hand, so it’s no surprise that the brand’s watches offer robust tracking and navigation. These features can be essential for runners, hikers, and outdoor athletes. Most Garmin watches provide detailed maps, turn-by-turn directions, and breadcrumb trails that help you retrace your steps. Some high-end models, like the aforementioned Fenix 8, offers offline maps with enhanced satellite imagery, SATIQ technology, ABC sensors, and more. These features can be invaluable for precise tracking even in steep valleys, offer reliable compass headings, and deliver accurate elevation readings.

Garmin watches traditionally prioritize function over fashion, packing them with a lot of tech and large batteries. As a result, they generally skew larger compared to many competitors. Some models come in multiple sizes—the Venu 4 is available with screen sizes of 41mm and 45mm, similar to the Apple Watch Series 11, which comes in 42mm and 46mm. However, the Venu 3 is still noticeably larger; it boasts a width of 45mm and a thickness of 12mm (compared to the Series 10’s 36mm and 9.7mm). That said, some of Garmin’s watches, like the Forerunner 970, only come in one size. If you have smaller wrists like I do, you have two options: Buy your preferred model and accept that it might look oversized on your wrist, or opt for one of Garmin’s more lifestyle-oriented models like the Vivoactive 6, which is 10.9mm thick. Garmin does offer "S" variants of several models specifically designed for small wrists—the Venu 3S, for example, is thinner and lighter than the normal Venu 3. However, these S models typically sacrifice battery life for their smaller footprint, so you’ll have to consider if that’s a compromise you’re willing to make.

There are a lot of Garmin watches to choose from—the brand lists five major lineups on its website. The Forerunner 165 is one of Garmin's most affordable models at $249, providing you essential training metrics, built-in GPS, and up to 11 days of battery life. The more full-featured Venu 4 jumps up in price to $549, offering more detailed health insights, better battery life, and a larger, more vibrant display. Garmin’s premium adventure watches command the highest prices, with the Fenix 8 starting at $899 and climbing to $1,099 for solar-equipped models with sapphire crystal displays. When deciding which Garmin is right for you, consider what features you truly need versus what’s nice to have. If you’re a casual runner, you might be best served by something in the Forerunner lineup. But if you regularly go hiking in the backcountry, you might find the premium price of a Fenix justified by its comprehensive navigation tools and extended battery life.

#4847. The 7 Best Microcurrent Devices of 2026 Tested by Women’s Health Editors

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

We’re living in the golden age of high-tech skincare devices—and as our beauty editor, I couldn’t be happier. Red light therapy devices, including LED face masks, provide excellent anti-aging benefits from the comfort of our couch, while face steamers have replaced my need for pricey spa facials. Laser hair removal devices are becoming more inclusive by offering technology safe enough for deeper complexions. Face massagers also help de-puff skin after a hangover. However, when it comes to lifting saggy skin, microcurrent devices are the ultimate MVP skincare tool deserving of a spot in your beauty arsenal.

Think of them as a sculpting workout for your face without the sweat. “Microcurrent devices use low levels of electrical current to stimulate facial muscles, helping to boost collagen and sculpt and lift the face,” says dermatologist Marisa Garshick, MD. And don’t worry: These aren’t painful. You’ll notice more of a temporary tingling sensation that’ll disappear within minutes of using the device.

While these at-home machines aren’t as powerful as the ones used by professionals, they’re a more cost-effective option for achieving subtle improvements, says dermatologist Bradley Glodny, MD. You’ll just need some patience to find a weekly cadence and intensity level that works for you. (More on that in a bit.) And if you’re getting seasonal in-office microcurrent treatments, these at-home machines help enhance and sustain your professional results over time, says Dr. Garshick.

What was once a closely guarded secret among my fellow beauty editors and plastic surgeons has now become increasingly popular and readily accessible across our most trusted sites, such as Sephora, Ulta, and Amazon. But an influx of hundreds of options can be overwhelming, which is where I come in. My years of reporting and research have informed this shopping guide. I also consulted the pros about what to look out for when buying at-home microcurrent machines. Ahead are a few non-negotiables to keep in mind, which helped inform the devices we tested and ultimately featured in this story.

Most devices on this list have a range of microcurrent levels—some, like Foreo, even go up to 10. The higher you go, the more intense the microcurrent will feel. If you're accustomed to microcurrent and prefer a device with more power and customization options, opt for one that offers multiple microcurrent levels.

On the other hand, if you're a beginner, you might only need to purchase a device with a few microcurrent levels, such as the NuFace Trinity.

Dr. Garshick advises using your microcurrent device at least three times a week for four to six weeks before you can expect to see results, although some devices recommend daily use. “While much of the initial benefit may only be noticed for hours to days, with consistent use, the results will continue as collagen production can take six or more months,” she says.

After the initial treatment period, you can decrease the frequency of treatments to two to three times per week to maintain your results. Always refer to the specific instructions for use of your microcurrent device.

Many microcurrent devices come with additional features, such as interchangeable attachments, smartphone app connectivity, and even instructional guides.

An added bonus for your microcurrent device is FDA approval, which means that the government organization has determined that the device is safe and effective for its intended use. This is not a necessity when purchasing a microcurrent device, but it's definitely a solid addition if you're looking for something that has been rigorously tested.

You’ll also want to order a microcurrent device that either includes a priming gel or purchase one separately. They’re conductive and allow the electrical currents to be transmitted from the device to the skin. They also help the device glide easily across the skin and help prevent irritation.

Unlike bulky in-office machines, at-home microcurrent devices are about the size of a closed fist. Someone who travels often might prefer the Solawave Facial Wand, a slim option that resembles a T-shaped salad fork. Regardless of which of these featured options you order, they won’t take up too much space in your medicine cabinet or cosmetic bag.

At-home microcurrent machines aren’t exactly cheap. Entry-level models cost around $150, while high-end options can easily go for upwards of $500. However, you’ll save money over time because you get multiple uses out of a single device. And if it helps ease the burden, I spent $275 for a pro microcurrent facial, which costs $60 more than the WH Skincare Award-winning Laduora Lumeo and conductive gel.

With the above dermatological guidance in mind, I began whittling down our list of contenders. The Women’s Health beauty closet was my first stop, along with my at-home collection of skincare devices. Of course, because I’m inquisitive and love knowing what the pros actually use IRL and recommend to their patients, I asked both Dr. Garshick and Dr. Glodny for their fail-safe picks. Next, I tapped our team of skin-obsessive editors and writers, including Brian Underwood, Lily Wohlner, Maridel Reyes, and Cristina Montemayor. And because we prefer only spotlighting products we actually tested, we put them all through a vetting process, which includes:

I eliminated anything that was cumbersome. For example, anything with a short cord or an extra-long one that easily tangled was cut. Were the cordless devices easy to charge quickly if I was in a crunch? Were there any other buttons or features that are easy to accidentally hit while rolling the device across my face?

These aren’t exactly short treatments. We’ll need at least a few minutes per treatment session, so caring for an entire face can easily take 15 minutes or more. I prioritized lightweight, but durable devices that easily slide across my skin. Anything that made my wrist tired after a few minutes was docked points. Was the tingling too intense for beginners or best suited for novices? Are there enough levels for both beginners and experienced users?

This was particularly important because everyone wants a lifted appearance. I evaluated if I noticed any improvements after the first usage, and kept checking in over the last six months. How do the results improve over time?

This was determined based on how each device scores in relation to the above factors. Plus, I asked myself and our team if these are products they’d be willing to repurchase or gift to loved ones because they stand behind the quality of the devices. Ultimately, each of these featured picks met those requirements; here are the results of our labor.

This NuFace device ticks all the boxes on my microcurrent wish list. The lifting effect smoothens the appearance of wrinkles and contours my cheekbones and jawline, even without makeup. The Trinity+ Starter Kit includes accessories to enhance my routine, such as a conductive gel that helps the NuFace glide smoothly across my skin. The device also comes with a lip and eye attachment, allowing me to target smaller problem areas, such as the 11 lines between the brows and smile lines.

This palm-sized powerhouse fits comfortably in my hands, and the five-minute treatment time was quick and easy. It doesn’t sting, and the tingling is mild as long as I use enough conductive gel. The Trinity also beeps, indicating when to move on to a new area of my face. I noticed results after just a few uses, which continued to improve after several months of consistent treatments.

Dr. Glodny and Dr. Garshick also both recommend this device. "This microcurrent device is FDA-cleared, helps to tone facial muscles, and improves the overall contour and appearance of the skin," says Dr. Garshick, adding that it can help rejuvenate the skin and improve skin laxity and the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles.

Honestly, the worst thing I can say about this is the upfront cost. However, I’ve had my device since 2020, and it still performs well six years later. For that reason alone, the NuFace is a long-term investment that delivers fast results that continue to improve over time.

When you have a tighter budget, look no further than the sub-$170 Solawave device, which has microcurrent, red light therapy, a facial massage setting, and therapeutic warmth. These settings are great for anti-aging and skin tightening, as well as reducing the look of hyperpigmentation and blemishes. Given its capabilities, the Solawave is comparable to devices that cost twice as much, including the TheraFace Pro. Purchasing the Solawave is also a power move, as you won’t need to purchase four devices to achieve similar results. Genius!

It’s also gone viral on social media and even earned snaps from the makeup artist for Vanessa Hudgens and the groomer for Pedro Pascal. Most importantly, it left a lasting impression on our team. I like using it in the morning when I want to depuff my face. Whenever I use this device, my skin feels firmer and looks dewy, especially when paired with the Solawave face serum. Together, the microcurrent and red light therapy have been especially helpful for smoothing my skin—it’s like a wrinkle-smoothing iron for my face.

The only downside about this rechargeable device is that it’s less powerful than other microcurrent devices. It only features one preset setting, but with consistent use, you’ll notice long-term improvements. However, if you’re a beginner, then you’ll appreciate the mild tingling.

Yes, this is the priciest option, but the capabilities are next-level great. This is, by far, the smartest microcurrent machine on this list. The Bluetooth-capable device has a smartphone app that allows you to choose from seven different facials, all ranging from four to 14 minutes long. Some focus on sculpting, while others zap acne, brighten your complexion, or smooth out fine lines. To unlock all available treatments, simply sync your device with the app.

Setting up the account on iOS or Android is straightforward, and it includes FAQ tutorials that guide you on how to use the device correctly. Each step of the Ziip device is broken down into easy-to-follow clips that remind you when to move on to a new section of the face for anti-aging benefits. One of my favorite treatments is called “Energize,” which starts at my neck and works its way up to my forehead in about 12 minutes.

It is also unique because Ziip combines microcurrent and nanocurrent technologies. Meanwhile nanocurrent is a low-intensity, sensitive skin-friendly way to reduce fine lines and enhance skin radiance.

Reyes also adores her ZIIP. "I used it every night, and after a few days, my husband noticed that my face looked more contoured," says Reyes. "The day after I use it, my skin looks smoother and glowier." She relies on it right before important events for more chiseled cheekbones, a sharper jaw, and a slightly lifted brow because it provides instant gratification and is "way less spendy than getting a microcurrent facial at a spa."

I’ve been using the Laduora Lumeo device since it was first released in 2025—and I’ve adored it so much over the past year that I named it the best new microcurrent tool in our 2026 Beauty Awards

So what makes it so worthy of a spot in your routine? For starters, it’s compact. It tucks nicely into my tightly edited cosmetic pouch and carry-on bag without adding extra bulk. TBH, it’s so effective and seamless to use that I’ve ditched my other bulky microcurrent devices and LED face masks in favor of this 4-in-1 device.

Microcurrent gently lifts and defines my cheekbones, while electroporation helps my face serum and cream penetrate more effectively. It also taps into red LEDs to soften my fine lines and wrinkles, while near-infrared light penetrates beneath my skin's surface, helping it feel firmer. Instead of splurging on multiple devices, I can easily get away with just using this single tool.

The best part? Zero downtime! I can rely on this travel-friendly device before special events without irritation, such as redness. Hello, wedding season prep. No wonder the celebrity makeup artists to Jenna Ortega and Naomi Watts rely on it to primp their clients before red carpet events. Need another reason to invest in this tool? It’s a kit that includes the conductive gel, so there’s no need to make a separate purchase. I have oily, acne-prone skin, and it has never caused breakouts.

TBH, it’s hard to pick a downside with this tool. However, if I had to nitpick, I’d like to see it in different colorways, like with the brand’s new microcurrent wands. Still, the functionality is on point, and it costs less than other devices on this list, including the TheraFace. And for that, Laduora will have a permanent spot in my beauty stash.

When you’re short on time, you’ll want to reach for this top-rated Foreo tool. A treatment with this device takes only two minutes, although you can follow up with additional sessions to target specific areas of the face. I like to concentrate on my cheekbones for an extra lift. It’s great for travel, and I found myself using this device more regularly than other devices because the treatments are so quick. The Bear doesn’t feel like a chore, and it's something I can easily use during commercial breaks on TV or while on the phone.

Both Dr. Garshick and Dr. Glodny recommend this cute palm-sized device, which firms and tones skin with microcurrent and massaging T-sonic pulsations that help with sagging skin, reduce puffiness, smooths wrinkles, and relaxes muscles. It's also an FDA-cleared device that boasts a proprietary anti-shock system that ensures you have a safe experience without compromising on results, says Dr. Garshick.

It even helps to relax tension in the face while promoting blood flow. After a few weeks of regular use, my face felt tighter and my eye areas looked more lifted and awake. Not only did my skin look better, but using this device also helped with relieving tension headaches. A single charge can provide 90 uses, so I can take it on the go to these Travel Award-winning destinations even if I forget to pack my charger.

The only downside? The tingling is still noticeable, even with the use of plenty of conductive gel, which means it’s working, but can also be a little uneasy. However, each treatment is only two minutes, so it’s not a deeply uncomfortable experience.

When I saw that this device offers eight treatments in one, I was initially skeptical that the microcurrent attachment wouldn’t be up to par with some of the other devices I tried. I was pleasantly surprised by how effective it was; I saw a difference after using the microcurrent for just a few minutes. But what really sold me was the combination of a powerful microcurrent skin toning device to lift the jowls, along with several magnetic attachments that amplify my skincare routine.

You’ve also got red light therapy and infrared lights to address wrinkles and fine lines, while blue LED light targets acne-causing bacteria. She’s a big fan of the various skin benefits, especially the trifecta of microcurrent, LED therapy, and cryotherapy. "It seems intimidating if you’re a beginner, but this tool truly makes my life so much easier for banishing acne, tightening my skin, and waking me up when I didn’t get enough sleep the night before,” says Wohlner.

Pesky adult acne and redness have been cosmetic concerns for Wohlner, but the TheraFace Pro has helped solve her skincare woes. She saw some initial glowy finish, but achieved the most visible anti-aging results after a few weeks of regular use.

While some microcurrent devices also relieve jaw tension, when using the percussion attachments in conjunction with the microcurrent, Wohlner found that her jaw muscles felt more relaxed and looked more toned than ever. The combination of those treatments in this single device truly sets it apart in terms of effectiveness. “I also struggle with jaw pain from grinding my teeth, and the percussive therapy this device offers is a major game-changer when I wake up with a sore jaw," says Wohlner.

You can’t go wrong with this tool, but if you won’t realistically incorporate at least a few of these modalities into your routine, it’s probably best to save some money and stick with a more affordable alternative. That said, we’re big fans and have gifted some to our lucky loved ones, including our moms, who are fine-tuning their mature skincare routines.

NYC eyebrow guru Joey Healy created the ultimate microcurrent for lifting the delicate skin around your eye area. It's not uncommon for your brows to start sagging with age, making your eyes appear droopier and more closed off. If you have hooded eyes, this effect is even more pronounced. This microcurrent device is made specifically to target the eyebrow area and tighten the skin around the browbone, giving hooded eyes a lifted, more awake appearance.

Montemayor gave this device a solid five stars because she noticed a noticeable difference in her eyebrows after using it. Even after her first go, her droopy eyebrow was even with her other one. She tells us that this device is super powerful; she can't even fathom using the highest level. Another reason to love this device? It automatically powers down after 15 minutes of use, preventing skin overstimulation and accidental battery drain.

The only downside of this device is that it uses batteries. While we wish it were rechargeable, this device is cordless, which is particularly helpful for anyone with limited outlets in their home.

Microcurrent devices aren't exactly cheap—the most affordable ones are still over $100, though the best ones tend to be around $300. Just be sure to use your device consistently at least three times a week, as Dr. Garshick mentioned.

If you're hesitant, she recommends chatting with your dermatologist about your skincare concerns and goals. They can help you come up with a treatment plan to supplement the use of your microcurrent device, optimizing the benefits of it.

#4846. The Ancient Secret to Calm and Courage

After years or decades, problems and patterns can become deeply entrenched. Be a fly on the wall during a sample couples therapy session and witness the slow, deliberate work of changing those patterns for a more enduring love.

Self Tests are all about you. Are you outgoing or introverted? Are you a narcissist? Does perfectionism hold you back? Find out the answers to these questions and more with Psychology Today.

Updated November 10, 2026 | Reviewed by Michelle Quirk

In 424 BCE, the Athenian army suffered a crushing defeat at Delium. As the soldiers fled the battlefield, one man stood out for his extraordinary composure. He was neither a famous general nor a celebrated warrior, but a middle-aged philosopher.

According to the officer Alcibiades, who witnessed the retreat from horseback, Socrates walked away with such calm and confidence that the enemy soldiers left him alone, preferring to pursue those who were fleeing in panic.

It was not the first time Socrates had distinguished himself in battle. Nor would it be the last.

We tend to picture Socrates as an old man in the marketplace, questioning his fellow Athenians about courage, justice, and the good life. But he did not merely talk about courage; he demonstrated it.

Like many Athenian citizens, Socrates trained as a hoplite, a heavily armed foot soldier who fought in the close formation known as the phalanx. He fought in at least three campaigns: Potidaea, Delium, and Amphipolis.

The earliest of these, the siege of Potidaea, began in 432 BCE, when Socrates was about 38 years old. The siege was long and arduous, with the soldiers exposed to hunger, cold, and disease.

In Plato’s Symposium, Alcibiades recalls that Socrates endured these hardships much better than anyone else in the army. During a severe frost, he marched barefoot over the ice, apparently indifferent to the cold. His comrades looked daggers at him, thinking that he was showing them up.

Yet, Socrates was no joyless ascetic. Alcibiades adds that no one enjoyed a festival more than he did. If called upon, he could drink everyone under the table—although no one had ever seen him drunk.

At Potidaea, Socrates also saved Alcibiades’ life. But when the generals awarded the prize for valour to the high-born Alcibiades, Socrates insisted that Alcibiades should keep it.

Here was a man who could endure almost anything, enjoy almost anything, and yet remain master of himself. No wonder Alcibiades was in love with him. To everyone's shock, Alcibiades even shared a tent with him.

It is hardly surprising that a man with so much experience of war should have thought deeply about courage.

In Plato’s Laches, Socrates discusses the nature of courage with two distinguished generals, Laches and Nicias.

At first, courage might seem easy enough to define. Surely, it consists in standing one’s ground against the enemy, or in remaining fearless in the face of danger?

But Socrates is not so sure. After all, a man might remain fearless out of foolishness or recklessness. He might be fearless simply because he does not understand the danger he is in. Would we call such a man courageous?

After a time, Nicias proposes that courage is a kind of knowledge: knowledge of what is truly to be feared and hoped for.

Socrates finds this definition more promising, but points out that such knowledge cannot be confined to the future. To know what is truly to be feared and hoped for, we must also know what is truly good and bad. Therefore, courage, if it is to be called courage, is born out of knowledge in general.

Socrates notices that, in trying to define courage, they have stumbled upon two larger ideas. First, the virtues are closely related. To be truly courageous, we must also be wise, just, and self-controlled. This is known as the unity of the virtues. Courage is not simply the ability to face danger, but the wisdom to know whether the danger ought to be faced. Second, deep down, all the classical virtues—courage, justice, piety, temperance—amount to knowledge and wisdom.

But is knowledge alone enough? Might it not be possible to understand what is right and true and still lack the courage to act upon it? For Socrates, if we truly know what is right and true, we cannot fail to act upon this knowledge. But in Plato’s Republic, courage takes on a further dimension: the preservation of our convictions about what is and is not to be feared, despite our desires, fears, and baser instincts. This, if you like, is a kind of meta-courage: the courage to remain faithful to one’s understanding of what matters.

As I discuss in my book, The Gang of Three, calm and courage begin with knowing what is truly worth fearing and meeting it with wisdom rather than fear. The less we depend on comfort, approval, and other things we might lose, the less we have to fear, and the more freely and courageously we can live.

In 399 BCE, Socrates was put on trial for impiety and corrupting the youth. Facing the possibility of execution, he refused to abandon philosophy or say what was needed to save his life.

Instead, he reminded the jury that, just as he had not deserted his post at Potidaea or Delium for fear of death, so he would not now desert his lifelong convictions.

For Socrates, to fear death was to pretend to know what we do not know. Death might be an evil, but it might equally be a blessing. What we do know is that injustice is an evil, and that it is better to suffer an injustice than to commit it.

When Socrates was condemned to death, he had the means to escape, but chose instead to drink of the poisoned cup.

With the same extraordinary composure, the man who had faced death for Athens now faced death at the hands of Athens. He had not merely talked about courage, or even demonstrated it on the battlefield. He had carried it through to the very end.

It’s quite a thought that, had Socrates fallen in battle, or, at the end, played the part of a coward, we today would be living in different minds, in a different world.

You may also enjoy my companion piece, Why Socrates Chose to Die.

Recreating that experience at home doesn't require another plane ticket. The Six Bells Countryside Inn opened its doors in the bucolic Hudson Valley in 2025, and it’s already earned two Michelin Keys. In each of the 11 carefully and whimsically designed bedrooms at this retreat, you’ll find handcrafted mattresses and bedding from New York-born brand Ostermoor. Dating back to 1853, Ostermoor’s mattresses have a storied history. The beds have innovated to foam and pocketed coil inner layers and designer covers in recent years, and we can prove they’re worth the splurge.

“From the moment I plopped down on the mattress, I was amazed by how comfortable and supportive it was,” shares contributor Zoë Sessums. “It strikes a perfect balance between spring and cushion—just the right amount of give without ever feeling too soft. I consistently wake up feeling rested and supported.” Firm without feeling rigid, this mattress looks as good as it feels, too. “The tufted top, the blue and white ticking pattern, the hand-stitched details—it feels like a piece of luxury furniture, not just a place to sleep,” Sessums adds, later writing, “I would recommend this to someone who values design and craftsmanship as much as comfort.”

Saatva has found its way into charming bed-and-breakfasts and boutique retreats across the country, including Pasadena's historic Bissell House (an 1887 Victorian filled with antique furnishings) and the Cornell Inn in the Berkshires (known for its colorful, individually designed guest rooms). You can bring that same inviting comfort home with the Saatva Classic, which comes with a plush three-inch Euro pillow top, a responsive dual-coil system, and targeted lumbar support. “It’s firm (which I prefer), regulates temperature well, and is extremely durable,” our tester Erin Kaplan, vice president of communications at Conde Nast, says. “I alternate between sleeping on my side and sleeping on my stomach, and this mattress is great for both positions.”

Choose from three firmness levels—plush soft, luxury firm, or firm—, eight different sizes, and two mattress heights to find your ideal fit. Feeling extra? Saatva also offers two adjustable bases that elevate your head and feet at the touch of a button, including a premium Plus model for an even more indulgent breakfast in bed. With custom Keetsa mattresses in every room, you might find yourself hitting snooze despite the spectacular view.

A three-inch pillow top combines body-contouring memory foam with responsive comfort foam to help cushion pressure points, and a soft, moisture-wicking cover designed to keep overheating at bay. Individually wrapped coils provide cushioning and support while minimizing motion transfer, so even if your bedmate tosses and turns, you can stay blissfully unaware.

When husband-and-wife duo Ely and Danielle Franko transformed a dated Catskills ski hostel into The Henson, a 16-room boutique hotel, they had a pretty good idea of what makes a great night's sleep. The couple painstakingly restored the property themselves, filling its rooms with vintage furniture, locally sourced finds, and hand-applied wallpaper. But when it came to mattresses, they didn't have to look far for inspiration: They chose the same Casper Dream Hybrid they sleep on at home. In fact, they loved it so much that they insisted on king-size mattresses in every room, even the smallest ones. The hybrid design combines responsive springs with breathable foam and three zones of support that help keep your spine aligned. Its medium feel is meant to offer a little give without leaving you sinking into the mattress, making it a crowd-pleasing choice for your own guest room. After all, the best hosts know a good night's sleep is part of the hospitality.

Hot sleepers, here’s a mattress for you. The Four Season’s signature mattress features a couple of core cooling bed qualities: proprietary cooling gel foam layers with channeled designs that promote airflow throughout the mattress, as well as a patented DualCool top layer that draws heat and moisture away from the body and keeps the bed fresh with its antimicrobial properties. The cooling mattress is designed for sleepers who need extra structure on their bed. This posh number has targeted support for the lower back area and zeroes in on alignment regardless of your sleep style.

The W Hotels are widely popular because of the bold design across the properties worldwide. To mirror this aesthetic, you can cover the brand’s mattress with colorful bedding to let your personal style shine. When it comes to the bed itself, it is defined by a plush top quilted damask design to ease side sleepers into a peaceful slumber. It’s made for people who need extra support too, though, including an individually-wrapped coil system, five-zone support system, and comfort layers for added cushioning and pressure relief.

Which Kind of Mattress Do Five-Star Hotels Use?

Most luxury hotels use hybrid mattresses in their suites to strike the right balance of softness and support, thanks to pocketed coils and layers of foam. These are also typically medium-firm mattresses since a plush mattress can be uncomfortable for some sleep positions like stomach sleepers. Ultra-firm beds are often too stiff for side sleeping and may not align with guests' expectations who are looking for soft mattresses to sink into on their vacations.

If you want to refresh your mattress without the hefty price tag of buying a new one, a mattress topper or featherbed could be a solid transitional pick. The Ritz-Carlton and W Hotels promote one made with white duck feathers, Mandarin Oriental’s exclusive topper comprises white goose feathers, Waldorf Astoria beds feature a down-alternative fill, and Marriott’s selection is polyester.

There’s no one-size-fits-all here, so it really comes down to your preferred loftiness and weight. Duck and goose feathers are heavier than others fills, though duck is slightly less fluffy and won’t trap heat as well. Down-alternatives, like polyester, are more allergen-friendly and “a good option for those who prefer to be vegan in their home,” Danielle Trotter, the former textiles technical designer at West Elm, previously shared.

What Is the Thickness of a Hotel Mattress?

Hotel mattresses usually average 12 inches in thickness. This makes it easier to hop in and out of bed, especially when using a box spring that can add extra height. Plus, it prevents the need for deep pocket sheets.

How Can I Recreate the Hotel Bed Experience at Home?

We’ve explored the entire topic on how to make your bedroom feel like a hotel, and aside from finding a new bed with a medium-firm feel, we’ve learned that percale sheets and down pillows are pretty much a must to complete the setup. When it comes to the former, hotel sheets are usually made with organic cotton percale because the fabric looks and feels crisp, giving that refined aesthetic a boutique stay is known for. Usually a 200 thread count is a good rule of thumb to look out for since this means there’s plenty of airflow between the threads for a breathable feel. Hotel pillows are usually filled with down feathers since they’re so lofty and soft, but a down alternative is just as good in case you’re an allergy-prone sleeper (just look for materials like hypoallergenic gel fibers since they’re known for being squishy without falling flat, just like a feather-filled pillow).

What Is the Difference Between Memory Foam and Latex?

Traditional memory foam has a body-contouring effect that allows your body to sink into your mattress, reducing motion transfer (a must for bedmates!). Meanwhile, latex foam offers more responsiveness (or bounce) and overall support. As Neslihan Ozdemir, founder of Girl on the Mattress, previously told AD, latex also holds up well over time and is temperature-regulating. Latex foam mattresses (and some memory foam options) are certified organic, making them eco-friendly foam picks, too.

Known as the most common mattress type, innerspring mattresses feature a bed of coils. There’s quite a range to these mattresses: Basic versions have a grid of steel coils, while premier options have a pillow top and pocketed coil technology, meaning each coil is individually wrapped to help with motion isolation. Ozdemir added that innerspring is best for people who sleep on the edge of the bed or are heavier in weight. If you prefer a more plush mattress, but still want the support of those coils, consider a hybrid mattress, which is layered with soft foam.

#4844. RJ Mitte's Death Highlights Mental Health Challenges for People With Cerebral Palsy

Follow Healthline on our socials for all things health.

“Breaking Bad” actor and disability advocate RJ Mitte has died at age 34.

Mitte reportedly died by suicide, his representative told People on October 12. However, local authorities have said the official cause and manner of his death remain under investigation.

Mitte, who was best-known for playing Walter White Jr. on the Emmy Award-winning television series “Breaking Bad,” lived with cerebral palsy and advocated for disability inclusion.

There is currently no evidence to suggest that cerebral palsy caused the actor’s death. Still, Mitte’s untimely passing highlights the mental health challenges that people with cerebral palsy may face.

Research has demonstrated elevated risks of anxiety and depression among those with the condition, alongside barriers to diagnosis, social participation, and employment.

“Living with cerebral palsy can affect mental health through several interacting pathways,” said Shannel Elhelou, neuropsychologist and founder of Brain Centric Neuropsychology in Westlake Village, CA.

“Chronic pain, fatigue, disrupted sleep, and the effort required to navigate daily activities can take an emotional toll. Experiences of bullying, discrimination, social exclusion, and difficulty accessing care can add to that burden. Also, the early brain injury underlying cerebral palsy may contribute to difficulties with emotional regulation, although each person’s experience is different,” Elhelou told Healthline.

If you or someone you know is in crisis and considering suicide or self-harm, please seek support:

If you’re calling on behalf of someone else, stay with them until help arrives. You may remove weapons or substances that can cause harm if you can do so safely.

If you’re not in the same household, stay on the phone with them until help arrives.

Mitte played a key role in challenging stereotypes by portraying a teenager with cerebral palsy on “Breaking Bad.”

Outside of acting, Mitte advocated for people with disabilities through organizations including United Cerebral Palsy (UCP) and Shriners Children’s.

He also led the Mitte Foundation, a non-profit corporation founded in 1994 by his grandparents, Roy F. and Joann Cole Mitte, that improves the quality of life for people in Central Texas.

Mitte’s advocacy emphasized representation, inclusion, and opportunities for people with disabilities.

The legacy he leaves behind underscores the need to recognize mental health as an essential part of care for individuals with cerebral palsy and other disabilities.

Cerebral palsy (CP) is a group of conditions affecting movement, posture, and coordination.

Most people with cerebral palsy have typical intelligence, although some also have intellectual disabilities or other comorbid physical and mental health conditions.

A 2018 study published in JAMA Neurology found that adults with cerebral palsy had a 28% higher risk of developing depression and a 40% higher risk of anxiety than adults without the condition.

A 2024 study in JAMA Network Open found higher recorded rates of anxiety and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) among children and young adults with cerebral palsy.

The researchers also identified comparatively low rates of depression and suicidal ideation, highlighting concerns that these conditions may be underdiagnosed.

“Research shows that adults with cerebral palsy have an increased risk of depression and anxiety,” Elhelou said.

“However, these conditions should never be viewed as an inevitable part of having a disability. One concern is ‘diagnostic overshadowing,’ when symptoms of depression, anxiety, or other mental health conditions are attributed to cerebral palsy itself, leading those conditions to go unrecognized and untreated. Someone’s fatigue, withdrawal, or changes in behavior deserve careful assessment rather than the assumption that ‘this is just their cerebral palsy,'” she continued.

“While these findings help us understand mental health risks among people with cerebral palsy, they cannot tell us what any one person was experiencing. Many interacting factors may contribute to someone dying by suicide, and it would be inappropriate to attribute an individual’s death to their disability.”

A 2019 study published in Developmental Medicine & Child Neurology found that children with cerebral palsy had higher odds of anxiety disorders and behavioral challenges than children without the condition.

Difficulties with friendships and bullying were associated with some of these differences.

Factors that may affect well-being include:

The researchers also found that supportive friendships may help reduce some of these disparities, reinforcing the importance of inclusive schools and communities.

A 2021 study published in the American Journal of Preventive Medicine found that U.S. adults with disabilities faced increased risks of suicidal thoughts, planning, and attempts compared with adults without disabilities.

The 988 Lifeline received more than 8 million contacts through calls, texts, chats, and American Sign Language videophone in 2025, according to the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration.

Federal funding for the Lifeline’s dedicated LGBTQ+ youth service ended in July 2025, removing the option to press 3 for specialized support.

After pressure from Congress, the service was recently restored at the end of September, according to the Kaiser Family Foundation (KFF).

Employment and financial independence can influence well-being for anyone, particularly those with cerebral palsy.

However, a 2024 study found that just 30.4% of young adults with cerebral palsy who participated in vocational rehabilitation programs were employed when they exited those programs.

Workplace accommodations, accessible hiring, vocational rehabilitation, and inclusive social opportunities can help address these barriers.

“Depression and anxiety are treatable, and they should never be dismissed as an inevitable part of living with a disability,” Elhelou said.

“If you notice persistent sadness, anxiety, hopelessness, or withdrawal, reach out to someone you trust and a mental health professional. You deserve a clinician who takes your concerns seriously and adapts treatment to your communication, mobility, or other access needs. Care should also address pain, fatigue, and sleep difficulties, which can affect emotional well-being.”

Organizations such as United Cerebral Palsy offer information and support for people with cerebral palsy and their families.

Healthcare professionals can also improve outcomes by screening for mental health concerns, using appropriate assessment tools, and connecting patients with accessible treatment.

Improved access to care, inclusive communities, and meaningful opportunities can help people with cerebral palsy and other disabilities thrive.

“Asking for help does not diminish your resilience or your contributions. If you are experiencing thoughts of suicide or feel overwhelmed, you do not have to wait until things feel unbearable to reach out,” Elhelou said.

“Supportive relationships, peer groups, and disability communities can offer connection and understanding. Staying engaged in activities that bring enjoyment and meaning can also help.”

#4843. 5 Ways to Handle Problems That Keep Coming Back

After years or decades, problems and patterns can become deeply entrenched. Be a fly on the wall during a sample couples therapy session and witness the slow, deliberate work of changing those patterns for a more enduring love.

Self Tests are all about you. Are you outgoing or introverted? Are you a narcissist? Does perfectionism hold you back? Find out the answers to these questions and more with Psychology Today.

Posted November 10, 2026 | Reviewed by Gary Drevitch

When I planted my fall garden here in Santa Barbara, I was most excited about the sunflowers. I had finally solved the problem of our ground squirrels. My bedroom window looks out over the garden, and now the sunflowers are a good five feet tall, with buds forming. When I wake up in the morning, they are the first thing I look for.

Except, smack in the middle of my view is some construction workers’ porta-potty.

Many mornings I look out there, hoping to see a sunflower, and instead I see an electrician exiting, pulling up his fly.

Such is our experience in life. Just as soon as we solve one problem, another one is blocking our way, interrupting our happiness.

Problems are like ground squirrels, and the construction workers, they keep coming back and you don’t get to decide when. So, what should we do when they do? Here are five things to consider, based on my Wise Effort method, and thousands of hours of listening to people’s problems (plus thousands of hours complaining about mine).

It wouldn’t be a problem if it didn’t matter to you in some deeper way. Try ranting about your problem for one minute (yes, set at timer) and then ask yourself: What does this reveal that I care about?

Now you have something more useful than a complaint. You have a direction.

Strange loops, vicious cycles, negative reinforcement, experiential avoidance, secondary gain—whatever psychological term you want to use, some problems stick around because they are solving other problems. How is your problem working for you? That construction worker is fixing my house, afte rall—and that fight you pick with your husband on Sunday night? It might just be serving you in some roundabout way too.

What is your struggle helping you avoid or what are you getting out of it?

Once you understand what the problem is doing for you, you have more freedom to choose another way.

Sometimes your problems keep coming back, because you are a problem search engine: You are only looking for things that are going wrong. Attention is like a spotlight. You can narrow it down to one tiny thing, or you can widen the lens and let it illuminate the whole picture. In Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, we call these processes flexible perspective-taking and flexible attention. When you can move your focus around—out and in, right and left, narrow and wide—how you see your problem will likely shift. Often it shifts toward something more balanced or compassionate.

The brain seeks stimulation, control, and something to do. And if there isn’t a problem available, it may create one. Life hands us problems, sure. But is it really a problem that the plane is late? Haven’t you been wanting, more than anything, a little time to do nothing? Is it really a problem that your teen is aloof? Aren’t you going to miss them when they are gone? Sometimes what is wrong is simply that your mind is looking for something wrong.

The word “acceptance” is in Acceptance and Commitment Therapy for a reason. Often the pathway to commitment and change is acceptance. Acceptance means allowing what is already here to be part of your experience so you can stop spending all your energy arguing with reality. It means making room for the full experience: irritation and gratitude, beauty and inconvenience, sunflowers and porta-pottys.

And sometimes, when you accept, move toward, and allow the very thing you fear or hate, you end up back at the beginning.

Beneath every problem is a value. As Pema Chödrön writes, “things come together and they fall apart.” Then they come together again. Then they fall apart again:

This week, choose one problem that has been taking up a lot of your energy

Your task is to become more skillful with the problems you have, so they can become gateways to your values and you can keep tending your little garden patch with care.

For more, see my book, Wise Effort: How to Focus Your Energy on What Matters Most; my interview with Eric Zimmer; or my weekly free mediation and Sangha.

#4842. The 10 Best Red Light Therapy Tools of 2026, Tested by Beauty Experts

Our top picks—from Omnilux, TheraFace, and Qure—treat acne, boost collagen, and more.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

If you're starting to notice that your skin is looking a little, well, tired, you're not alone. The visible signs of aging—I’m talking fine lines and wrinkles, dullness, even sallow skin—will strike us all sooner or later. Bummer. On the bright side, we're living in an age when there's no shortage of smart beauty devices and skincare products for these issues. From wrinkle-smoothing injections like Botox and fillers to anti-aging creams, you've got an arsenal of skin-boosting tools at your disposal.

But what if I were to tell you that there's one such solution that takes roughly 10 a day and can be done while you're relaxing in bed scrolling TikTok? Enter red light therapy.

Red light therapy has exploded in popularity lately because it's convenient, noninvasive, and can be done at home. It uses a specific spectrum of visible light that offers a host of beauty benefits—low-level laser light therapy can effectively treat scars, vitiligo, and psoriasis, research shows. It has an anti-inflammatory effect and can even help to smooth wrinkles, too. So, how does it work? We know that red light penetrates 2 to 3 millimeters into skin's dermis, where it's “absorbed by light-sensitive porphyrins in the mitochondria of skin cells, stimulating energy production in fibroblasts to churn out more collagen,” says dermatologist Ava Shamban, MD.

But the goodness doesn't stop there. Red light can also help fade dark spots and manage eczema, plus boost hair growth, says dermatologist Purvisha Patel, MD. These at-home devices can be expensive, but they're an investment you can use for a years to come: Many red light therapy tools are also equipped with blue lights, which are particularly effective at treating acne (say buh-bye to those period or menopausal breakouts) and other concerns. Bottom line: At any age—and for years to come—these red light therapy tools can be a beneficial addition to your beauty routine.

Ultimately, these are the devices that we’ll continue to use and would genuinely repurchase if we had to start our skincare routine from scratch. The best part? Our faves start at just $72, which is a major win for a category that easily ranges from $300 to $700.

I've got a great list of options for you, but if you find yourself in the market for a red light therapy tool, here are a few things to keep in mind.

There are several kinds of red light therapy devices to choose from, including panels, masks, and facial wands, and one may be a better fit for you based on your lifestyle and the area you're seeking to treat.

LED masks are the most common variety you'll find for home use because most are hands-free and contain a lot of diodes (a fancy way of referring to the individual lightbulbs), offering a powerful burst of light to treat the face, neck, or chest.

Maybe you're claustrophobic and the idea of wearing masks gives you the heebie-jeebies—that's where panels come in. They look like flexible bodyboards that you lie down under, and they come in a diverse range of shapes and sizes, each offering different levels of red light exposure to your face, décolletage, and back. These also help replace the need for a separate lip-specific red light therapy tool.

Wands are appealing when you want to target smaller specific areas (the crow's feet or smile lines, for example) and prefer to do your treatments on the go (you can walk around while using these).

Our eyes are the first place to show signs of aging, so you’ll want to take a cue from dermatologist Pooja Rambhia, MD, and use these affordable red light therapy eye tools. Red, deep red, and near-infrared wavelengths target fine lines, wrinkles, darkness, and puffiness early on, making them a smart preventive beauty move.

It's tempting to pick a device with the quickest treatment window, especially if you don't have loads of free time to sit back and chill with a red light mask. But remember: To treat more advanced signs of aging, a longer treatment time may be more beneficial. Look at the full picture before you base your purchase on the convenience of a quicker treatment. And for what it’s worth, almost all of our featured recommendations can be used in just three minutes, so even busy women can incorporate quick treatments into their routine.

You may notice the abbreviation nm on the outer packaging of many of these tools. This stands for nanometers and refers to the wavelength of the light that the device emits—an important metric to consider, says dermatologist Jody A. Levine, MD. "Red light typically falls between 630 and 660 nanometers, and is good for targeting fine lines and mild discoloration," says Dr. Levine. If you're looking for something slightly more powerful—to deal with deeper wrinkles, sagging, or stubborn pigmentary problems—go with a device that cranks up to the near-infrared range (between 800 and 850 nanometers) to penetrate deeper.

In addition to two types of red light—red and deep red—for anti-aging benefits, the mask also boasts infrared, amber, and blue lights to deal with acne, fine lines, and sun spots.

Using the device is simple: Hold down the power button for three seconds until the light turns on, adjust the straps, and press the button once for the anti-aging mode or press it twice for the acne treatment. You can also use the smartphone app to customize a plan just for you. The icing on the cake? Treatment time is only three minutes for all plans—among the fastest of all the devices we tested.

Qure's various LED lights are within the correct wavelength range to treat multiple skin concerns. For example, acne-fighting blue light should be between 400 and 500nm (Qure's is 415nm), while near-infrared is most helpful between 760 and 1,400nm.

In our evaluations, Earley loved the structure of the mask, which sits squarely on her face so it doesn’t need to be constantly readjusted (an annoying feature of some of the others we tried). "This mask is lightweight, and fit my face perfectly, making me feel like I was reaping the most benefits," says Earley.

The upfront investment for the Qure device has been well worth it for Metzger, who tested the Qure Light Therapy Mask for three weeks. "It’s simple, fast, and effective enough to become a daily habit—and that consistency is everything [when] it comes to skincare,” she said in her review. Metzger considers it an excellent complement to her skincare routine and is a proactive way for her to address her mature skin concerns.

On the downside, the customization component overcomplicated things, said Metzger. Qure has a compatible smartphone app that’s useful, but Metzger admitted it has a learning curve. “I found tinkering with it to be too time-consuming and defeated my favorite aspects of simplicity and speed," she said. This isn’t a huge dealbreaker for Metzger since she enjoys using the standard anti-aging mode.Qure LED Face Mask Review

Boasting a 4.1-star average from nearly 1,300 Amazon reviews—780 are perfect 5-star ratings—this popular red light therapy tool is worth owning, according to Men’s Health associate health and fitness editor Jocelyn Solis-Moreira. The setup instructions were easy for Solis-Moreira to follow. “I love that they idiot-proofed it. All I had to do was connect three pieces,” she says. Solis-Moreira adds that the elastic band was super helpful for keeping her device locked in place.

Don’t worry: it automatically powers down after each setting, making it practical for busy women looking for skin benefits without overthinking the process.

Crunched for time? Same! In just three minutes, Solawave emits a powerful blend of four LED wavelengths—red, near-infrared, deep red, and amber—to smooth lines on my décolletage. The mask features a high density of LEDs—320 to be exact—meaning my skin is basking in vibrant wavelengths with minimal gaps for ample coverage. After a month, my skin is glowing. So what else makes Solawave the hot topic of my group chat? Many brands sell LED masks only for the chest, but Solawave covers both my décolletage and neck. This device is still worth using—I saw a literal glow-up within my first month of use, and it only got better with time.

Boasting a 4.5/5 star rating from nearly 350 reviews, this red light therapy device is beloved by Amazon shoppers for its ability to offer cosmetic benefits and support your at-home recovery.

This tool is unique because it boasts an overhead display of 287 rows of light diodes and a 180-degree light source that provides a nearly 360-degree treatment for your face, neck, hands, and body. Purple LED light therapy combines red and blue light, meaning it offers benefits, like acne treatment, reduced inflammation, and improved overall skin health, making it a versatile option for skincare, says Dr. Spizuoco. Lastly, she highlights the unique white LED as a win since it uses the full spectrum of visible light which reduces fine lines and evens skin tone.

One of the best benefits of a panel like this is that you can use it on different areas of your body if you’re dealing with back or chest acne. The TheraFace Pro offers just about everything: multiple types of light therapy, percussive massage, microcurrent skin-toning, and cleansing. It's all possible thanks to eight different attachments that adhere to the head of the device via powerful magnets.

The highly versatile pick garnered high praise from Wohlner, but it didn't land our top spot because it's not hands-free, so we couldn’t take advantage of multitasking or the flexibility to relax during treatments. Zitz is also a big fan of her Theraface Pro, which she's been using on a weekly basis for two years. If you don't mind manually holding the device to your face, Wohlner says it offers an excellent value. She uses it to treat persistent acne or redness. And using the device is incredibly easy. Wohlner snaps on the blue or red light rings and watches her zits shrink within a week. The percussive therapy also relieves Wohlner’s jaw tension caused by grinding her teeth.

Unfortunately, the brand doesn't list exact treatment time, which makes the process a little ambiguous. However, Wohlner uses the device for about eight minutes. Start at the center of the chin and glide with light pressure upward to your right ear, then slide it back and forth until you finish each quadrant of your face. She wishes the directions were a bit clearer here, but if you want a truly multipurpose device, then this is the one for you.

Although this pick is expensive, it’s FDA-cleared and built to last for years, says dermatologist Shari Sperling, DO. She appreciates that it's equipped with both blue light for acne and red for aging skin.
